MR. JUSTICE SUJIT NARAYAN PRASAD HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE SANJAY PRASAD
For the Appellant : Mr. Awnish Shankar, Advocate For the Respondent : Mrs. Priya Shrestha, Spl.PP ------
th Order No.05/Dated: 7 February, 2025 I.A. No. 22 of 2025 1.

The instant interlocutory application has been filed under Section 430(1) of BNSS, 2023 for keeping the sentence in abeyance in connection with the judgment of conviction dated 02.09.2023 and order of sentence dated 08.09.2023 passed by the learned Additional Sessions Judge-1-cum- Special Judge (POCSO) Act, West Singhbhum at Chaibasa in connection with Special POCSO Case No.55 of 2020, whereby and whereunder, the appellant has been convicted under sections 376(3)
and 506 of the IPC and under Section 4(2) and Section 6 of POCSO Act and sentenced to undergo RI for 25 years and a fine of Rs.20,000/- for the offence under section 4(2) of the POCSO Act and in default of payment of fine further directed to undergo SI for one year.

entities.text: Additional Sessions Judge-1-cum- Special Judge (POCSO) Act, West Singhbhum at Chaibasa
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
The appellant has been further awarded sentence of RI for 30 years and a fine of Rs.30,000/- /- for the offence under section 6 of the POCSO Act and in default of payment of fine, further directed to undergo SI for additional two years.
2. It has been contended on behalf of the applicant that the applicant has falsely been implicated in the present case due to previous animosity, since, the same has been surfaced during the course of the trial on the basis of the testimony of the witnesses.

It has been contended that the testimony of Harilal Bodra @ Lomba Bodra vs The State Of Jharkhand on 7 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/16505936/
1 the victim is, therefore, not reliable, since, she with the malice mind has instituted the present case and supported the prosecution version only for the purpose of implicating the present applicant in a false case.
3. The learned counsel has further submitted by questioning the DNA profile test where it has come that a baby took birth from the womb of the present victim and the present applicant is the biological father of that child.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
But the said report cannot be said to be admissible in evidence, since,
the sample of blood of the applicant after keeping it for seven months had been sent to the FSL.
The learned counsel, based upon the aforesaid grounds, has submitted that it is a fit case for suspension of sentence.
4. While, on the other hand, Mrs. Priya Shrestha, learned Spl.PP appearing for the respondent-State of Jharkhand has vehemently opposed the prayer for suspension of sentence.
5. It has been contended by the learned Spl.PP that during trial the victim as PW1 has fully supported the prosecution version.

It has also been submitted that the age of the victim, at the time of occurrence, was of 14 years and she was subjected to the sexual assault resulting into birth of a baby child which has also been corroborated in the DNA test certifying therein that the applicant is the biological father of that child.
The doctor has also supported the prosecution version while examining as PW3.
Therefore, the learned Spl.PP, based upon the aforesaid grounds, has submitted that it is not a fit case for suspension of sentence.

6. We have heard the learned counsel for the parties and gone across the findings recorded by the learned trial Court in the impugned judgment as well as the testimony available in the lower Court records, as also the materials exhibit as available therein.
7.

This Court, after going through the testimony of the victim (PW1), whose age has been assessed to be of 14 years at the time of occurrence, has found that she has fully supported the prosecution version.
It is also evident from the materials available on record that the victim has given birth to a baby child who has been found to be of the present applicant on the basis of the DNA profile test.
This fact is corroborated by the testimony of the doctor who deposed as PW3 during the trial.
8. Therefore, we are not inclined to enlarge the present applicant on bail by suspending his sentence.
9. Accordingly, I.A. No. 22 of 2025 stands dismissed.

10. It is made clear that any observation made hereinabove will not prejudice the case on merit,
since, the criminal appeal is lying pending before this Court for its consideration.

11. Before parting with the order, the learned Member Secretary, JHALSA is directed to take endeavour with respect to the issue of taking care of the victim and her child by issuing specific direction to the concerned Chairman/Secretary of the District Legal Service Authority.
